nodes.title: A_inf, B_inf, B_dR^+ and B_dR of a perfectoid affinoid (K, K^+)-algebra; the element ξ
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 with an open bounded valuation subring K^+, and fix π ∈ K♭ with π♯/p ∈ (K^+)^×. For a perfectoid affinoid (K, K^+)-algebra (R, R^+) set A_inf(R, R^+) = W(R♭+), B_inf = A_inf[1/p], B_dR^+(R, R^+) = lim B_inf/(ker θ)^i. There is ξ ∈ A_inf(K, K^+) of the form ξ = [π] − Σ_{i≥1} p^i [x_i] (x_i ∈ K♭+; the source writes x_i ∈ O_{K♭}, but ξ must lie in W(K♭+), and writing π♯ = p·u with u ∈ (K^+)^× and lifting u through the surjection θ: W(K♭+) → K^+ produces x_i ∈ K♭+) generating ker(θ: A_inf(K, K^+) → K^+); ξ is not a zero-divisor, hence unique up to a unit, and for every (R, R^+) the same ξ generates ker(θ: A_inf(R, R^+) → R^+) and is a nonzerodivisor there. Consequently B_dR(R, R^+) := B_dR^+(R, R^+)[ξ^{-1}] carries the filtration Fil^i = ξ^i B_dR^+ with gr^i B_dR(R, R^+) ≅ ξ^i R, a free R-module of rank 1, and gr^• B_dR(R, R^+) ≅ R[ξ^{±1}].
hypotheses: K perfectoid of characteristic 0 with open bounded valuation subring K^+; π ∈ K♭ with π♯/p ∈ (K^+)^× (so π ∈ K♭+ is topologically nilpotent); (R, R^+) a perfectoid affinoid (K, K^+)-algebra in the field-based sense of Sch12. The proof uses that R♭+ is flat over K♭+ and that W(R♭+) and R^+ are p-torsion free (R^+ flat over Z_p).

Surjectivity of θ: W(R♭+) → R^+ is recalled, not proved ("Moreover, we know that θ ... is surjective", line 2037). Its supplier is PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel. The construction of ξ needs this surjectivity for (K, K^+).
The generation step uses W(R♭+)/(ξ, p) = R♭+/π = R^+/p, i.e. the tilting identification R♭+/π ≅ R^+/π♯ with π♯ ∈ p(K^+)^×. Its supplier is PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring.
proofSteps: Construction: θ([π]) = π♯ = p·u with u ∈ (K^+)^×; write u = θ(Σ_{j≥0} p^j [u_j]) with u_j ∈ K♭+ and put x_i = u_{i-1}, so that ξ = [π] − Σ_{i≥1} p^i [x_i] ∈ ker θ. (Packet-authored expansion of "any such element can be written as a sum Σ p^i θ([x_i])".)
Nonzerodivisor: if ξy = 0 with y = Σ p^i [y_i] ≠ 0, p-torsion-freeness of W(R♭+) lets one assume y_0 ≠ 0; reducing mod p gives πy_0 = 0 in R♭+, impossible since R♭+ is flat over K♭+.

Generation: for y ∈ ker θ, first reduce to y_0 ≠ 0 using p-torsion-freeness of W(R♭+) and R^+. W(R♭+)/(ξ, p) = R♭+/π = R^+/p gives z_0 with y − z_0ξ = p·y_1, and y_1 ∈ ker θ because R^+ is p-torsion free (the printed "f is mapped to zero" means y). Iterating gives y − (Σ_{i≤k} p^i z_i)ξ ∈ p^{k+1}W(R♭+), and p-adic completeness and separatedness of W(R♭+) give y = (Σ p^i z_i)ξ.
Corollary 6.4: ξ has the same properties in B_inf, so gr^i B_dR(R, R^+) = ξ^i B_dR^+/ξ^{i+1} B_dR^+ ≅ ξ^i R (the source says only "The corollary follows").
acceptance: For (R, R^+) = (C, O_C), ξ generates ker θ ⊂ A_inf, and B_dR^+(C) = lim A_inf[1/p]/ξ^i with gr^i = Cξ^i. That this is Fontaine's ring is true by definition but not discussed in the source; this is also the case where the node must agree with AInfCohomology:AI.0:integral up to a unit.

The element t = log([ε]) ∈ Fil^1 B_dR^+(K, K^+), for K = completed Q_p(μ_{p^∞}), generates Fil^1, and Gal(Q_p(μ_{p^∞})/Q_p) acts on it through the cyclotomic character. The proof of Proposition 6.7 recalls this without proof, so a test must supply its own derivation.

nodes.title: Structure sheaves O_X, O_X^+, Ô_X^+, Ô_X on X_proet and the continuous valuations on their sections
nodes.statement: For a locally noetherian adic space X over Spa(Q_p, Z_p), define on X_proet the uncompleted structure sheaf O_X = ν^* O_{X_et} with O_X^+ = ν^* O^+_{X_et}, the integral completed structure sheaf Ô_X^+ = lim O_X^+/p^n and Ô_X = Ô_X^+[1/p]. For U ∈ X_proet: every x ∈ |U| gives a continuous valuation f ↦ |f(x)| on O_X(U) which extends to Ô_X(U); O_X^+(U) = {f ∈ O_X(U) : |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} and Ô_X^+(U) = {f ∈ Ô_X(U) : |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}, so Ô_X^+(U) ⊂ Ô_X(U) is integrally closed; O_X^+/p^n → Ô_X^+/p^n is an isomorphism of sheaves and Ô_X^+(U) is flat over Z_p and p-adically complete.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian adic over Spa(Q_p, Z_p); U qcqs with a pro-etale presentation U = lim U_i (assertions are local in U).

The pro-etale site is Scholze's Definition 3.9 with the erratum's corrected notion of covers (transfinite compositions of pullbacks of finite etale surjections; unchanged for countable limits); the category X_proet itself is unchanged.

It is not known whether O_X(U) is dense in Ô_X(U) for arbitrary U, nor whether (|U|, Ô_X|_{|U|}, valuations) is always an adic space (remark after Lemma 4.2); both hold on the basis of affinoid perfectoid U.
proofSteps: (i) O_X(U) = colim O_X(U_i), and a point x is a compatible system of points x_i, so the valuations on O_X(U_i) combine.
(ii) For i large, |U| → |U_i| is surjective, so |f(x)| ≤ 1 on |U| forces |f_i(x_i)| ≤ 1 on |U_i| and f_i ∈ O_X^+(U_i).

(iii) formal from flatness of O_X^+ over Z_p. (iv) Define |f(x)| via max(|f_n(x̃)|, |p|^n) over local lifts, which is independent of the lift. (v) For qcqs U, Ô_X(U) = Ô_X^+(U)[1/p]; reduce to showing that |f(x)| ≤ |p|^n everywhere implies f ∈ p^n Ô_X^+(U). On a cover Ũ write f = f_0 + p^n g with f_0 ∈ O_X^+(Ũ) and g ∈ Ô_X^+(Ũ) (the source prints "g ∈ p^n Ô_X^+(Ũ)", a misprint), apply (ii) to f_0/p^n, and glue.
acceptance: For qcqs U ∈ X_et, O_X(U) = O_{X_et}(U) (Lemma 3.16 with i = 0; statement read by the reviewer). For U that is not affinoid perfectoid, no test may assume that O_X^+(U)/p^n → Ô_X^+(U)/p^n is an isomorphism or that Ô_X^+(U) is the p-adic completion of O_X^+(U): the remark after Lemma 4.2 says this is not known. Both hold on affinoid perfectoid U (Lemma 4.10(iii)-(iv)).
The valuations on Ô_X(U) are continuous for the topology with basis p^n Ô_X^+(U).

nodes.title: Affinoid perfectoid objects of X_proet, the functor U ↦ Û, and stability under etale and pro-etale maps
nodes.statement: Over a perfectoid field K of characteristic 0 with open bounded valuation subring K^+, and X locally noetherian over Spa(K, K^+): U ∈ X_proet is affinoid perfectoid if it has a pro-etale presentation U = lim U_i by affinoids U_i = Spa(R_i, R_i^+) such that, with R^+ the p-adic completion of colim R_i^+ and R = R^+[1/p], (R, R^+) is a perfectoid affinoid (K, K^+)-algebra; Û := Spa(R, R^+) is independent of the presentation, Û ~ lim U_i in the sense of Sch12 Definition 7.14 and |Û| = |U|. (Lemma 4.5) If V_i → U_i is etale, a composite of rational subsets and finite etale maps, then V = V_i ×_{U_i} U is affinoid perfectoid with V̂ = V_i ×_{U_i} Û and, for A_j the p-adic completion of the p-torsionfree quotient of S_j^+ ⊗_{R_j^+} R^+, S = A_j[1/p], the cokernel of A_j → S^+ is killed by a power of p, and for every ε > 0 in log Γ it is killed by p^ε for j large. (Lemma 4.6, Cor. 4.7) Anything pro-etale over a perfectoid U is perfectoid, and for X smooth over Spa(K, K^+) the affinoid perfectoid U form a basis of X_proet; Prop. 4.8 (Colmez) extends the basis statement to all locally noetherian X.
hypotheses: K a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 with open bounded valuation subring K^+; X locally noetherian over Spa(K, K^+). The source works over such K "for simplicity" (p. 22). By Remark 4.11 and Proposition 3.15, an affinoid perfectoid basis exists for every locally noetherian adic space over Spa(Q_p, Z_p).

Lemma 4.5 imports Sch12 Theorem 6.3(ii) (rational localizations of perfectoid affinoids are perfectoid), Lemma 6.4 (the subalgebras R^+⟨(f_i♯/g♯)^{1/p^m}⟩ with p^ε-bounded cokernel), Theorem 7.9(iii) (almost purity: S_j ⊗_{R_j} R perfectoid and uniformly almost finitely generated), Lemma 7.3(iv) and Proposition 7.10 (fibre products of finite etale maps).

Corollary 4.7 uses that a smooth X locally admits an etale map to the torus T^n (Huber [12] Corollary 1.6.10, unread) and the explicit cover T̃^n = lim Spa(K⟨T_i^{±1/p^m}⟩, K^+⟨T_i^{±1/p^m}⟩) of Example 4.4.

Asserted without proof in the passage read: independence of Û from the presentation and functoriality ("One immediately checks"); Û ~ lim U_i with |Û| = |U|; that A^+ is open and bounded for perfectoid affinoid (A, A^+) ("Recall"); the universal property of rational localization identifying (T, T^+) with the completion of (T_j, T_j^+); surjectivity of W → V_j for j large; and, in Lemma 4.6, that the completion of a direct limit of perfectoid affinoid (K, K^+)-algebras is perfectoid affinoid.

Proposition 4.8 (statement only) is proved by reducing to K algebraically closed through Proposition 3.15 and following Colmez [6] §4.4 and Lemma 1.15(iii) (sympathetic algebras are perfectoid); none of these were read.
proofSteps: Rational case: W is the pullback of the rational subset to Û, and (T, T^+) = (O_Û(W), O_Û^+(W)) is perfectoid affinoid by Sch12 Theorem 6.3(ii). With R_j0 ⊂ R_j^+ open bounded and S_j0 = R_j0⟨f_1/g, ..., f_n/g⟩, give T_j = S_j ⊗_{R_j} R the topology making the image of S_j0 ⊗_{R_j0} R^+ open and bounded, and let T_j^+ be the integral closure of the image of S_j^+ ⊗_{R_j^+} R^+. Then Spa(T_j, T_j^+) = V_j ×_{U_j} Û, and (T, T^+) is the completion of (T_j, T_j^+). Since T_j^+ is open and bounded, this topology is the one making the image of S_j^+ ⊗ R^+ open and bounded, so T = A_j[1/p], and boundedness of T^+ gives the p-power bound on the cokernel.
S^+ = T^+: injectivity of S_j^+/p^n → T^+/p^n for j large (W → V_j surjective) and surjectivity by approximating p^N f by elements of S_j^+ modulo p^{n+N} and dividing by p^N.
p^ε-bound: exhibit topologically finitely generated R^+-subalgebras T_ε^+ ⊂ T^+ with p^ε-torsion cokernel (Sch12 Lemma 6.4) and approximate their generators from S_j^+.

Finite etale case: T = S_j ⊗_{R_j} R is perfectoid by almost purity, Spa(T, T^+) is the fibre product by Sch12 7.3(iv)/7.10, and T^{+a} = T°a is uniformly almost finitely generated over R°a (7.9(iii)), giving the p^ε-bound.

Lemma 4.6: factor V → U as an inverse limit of finite etale surjections over an etale V_0 → U; each finite etale piece comes from a finite level and completed direct limits of perfectoid affinoids are perfectoid affinoid.
acceptance: T̃^n ∈ (T^n)_proet is affinoid perfectoid with (T̃^n)^ = Spa(K⟨T_i^{±1/p^∞}⟩, K^+⟨T_i^{±1/p^∞}⟩).

No example is worked in the source. A reviewer-authored test of Lemma 4.5(ii)-(iii) must use a nonempty rational subset of the torus, e.g. {|T_1 − 1| ≤ |p|} ⊂ T^1; {|T| ≤ |p|} is empty on T^n since |T_i| = 1 there. Check that the exponent N with p^N killing coker(A_j → S^+) can be taken to tend to 0 as j grows.

nodes.title: Ô_X^+(U) = R^+ and almost vanishing of H^i(U, Ô_X^+) for affinoid perfectoid U
nodes.statement: Let U ∈ X_proet be affinoid perfectoid with Û = Spa(R, R^+), in the almost setting for K^+ and its ideal of topologically nilpotent elements. Then (i) O_X^+(U)/b = R^+/b for nonzero b ∈ K^+, and this is almost equal to (O_X^+/b)(U); (ii) the image of (O_X^+/b_1)(U) in (O_X^+/b_2)(U) equals R^+/b_2 when |b_1| < |b_2|; (iii) Ô_X^+(U) = R^+ and Ô_X(U) = R; (iv) Ô_X^+(U) is the p-adic completion of O_X^+(U); (v) H^i(U, Ô_X^+) is almost zero for i > 0. In particular for perfectoid U, (|U|, Ô_X|_{|U|}, valuations) is the perfectoid space Û. (Lemma 3.18) If for an inverse system F_i, i ∈ N, of abelian sheaves on a site there is a basis B with R^1 lim F_i(U) = 0 and H^j(U, F_i) = 0 (j > 0) for U ∈ B, then R^j lim F_i = 0 for j > 0, (lim F_i)(U) = lim F_i(U), and H^j(U, lim F_i) = 0 for U ∈ B, j > 0.
hypotheses: U affinoid perfectoid; covers of U may be assumed to be a single V = lim V_j → V_{j'} → U with V_{j'} a composite of rational embeddings and finite etale maps and V_j → V_{j'} finite etale surjective (uses the corrected covering notion and quasicompactness of U).

Imports: giving a sheaf on X_proet is equivalent to giving a presheaf on affinoid perfectoid objects with the sheaf property for pro-etale covers by such (Proposition 4.8/Corollary 4.7); Lemma 4.5 (Čech complex of the cover is that of the etale cover V̂ → Û); Sch12 Proposition 7.13 (H^i(W_et, O^{+a}_W) = 0 for affinoid perfectoid W); the almost version of Lemma 3.18. The "almost version of Lemma 3.18" used for (v) is neither stated nor proved in the source.
proofSteps: (i) F(U) := (O^+(Û)/b)^a is a sheaf with vanishing higher cohomology: reduce the Čech complex of a cover V → U to a direct limit of Čech complexes of etale covers V̂_j → Û, which are almost exact by Sch12 7.13; hence F = (O_X^+/b)^a.
(ii) For f ∈ (O_X^+/b_1)(U) and c = b_1/b_2, c f = g comes from R^+ by (i); by valuations g = c h with h ∈ R^+, and injectivity of c: O_X^+/b_2 → O_X^+/b_1 gives f ≡ h in (O_X^+/b_2)(U).
(iii) Ô_X^+(U) = lim (O_X^+/p^n)(U) = lim R^+/p^n = R^+ by (ii); invert p for Ô_X(U) = R.
(iv) follows from (iii) and the definition of R^+ as the completion of colim R_i^+.

(v) By the proof of (i), H^i(U, O_X^+/p^n) is almost zero for all n > 0 and i > 0; the source concludes "from the almost version of Lemma 3.18" without more. The needed almost vanishing of R^1 lim on the basis (transition maps on sections almost surjective, from (ii)) is a packet-authored justification.
acceptance: For U = T̃^n, Ô_X(U) = K⟨T_i^{±1/p^∞}⟩ and H^i(U, Ô_X^+) is almost zero for i > 0.
The statement is 'almost equal' in (i) and 'equal' in (iii): passing to the inverse limit over n removes the almost defect using (ii).

nodes.title: The pro-etale period sheaves A_inf, B_inf, B_dR^+, B_dR and their filtrations
nodes.statement: On X_proet for X locally noetherian over Spa(Q_p, Z_p): A_inf = W(Ô^+_{X♭}) with B_inf = A_inf[1/p] and θ: A_inf → Ô_X^+ extending to θ: B_inf → Ô_X; B_dR^+ = lim B_inf/(ker θ)^n with Fil^i B_dR^+ = (ker θ)^i B_dR^+; B_dR = B_dR^+[t^{-1}] for any local generator t of Fil^1 B_dR^+, with Fil^i B_dR = Σ_{j∈Z} t^{-j} Fil^{i+j} B_dR^+. Locally on X_proet the element t exists, is unique up to a unit and is not a zero-divisor, so B_dR and its filtration are well defined.
hypotheses: Ô^+_{X♭} = lim_Φ O^+_X/p, the inverse limit along Frobenius, defined as a sheaf on all of X_proet (Definition 5.9, p. 33, read by the reviewer); over Spa(K, K^+), Ô_{X♭} = Ô^+_{X♭} ⊗_{K♭+} K♭. On affinoid perfectoid U its values are R♭+ and R♭, with almost vanishing higher cohomology (Lemma 5.10, whose proof only says to repeat part of the proof of Lemma 4.10 in the tilted situation). The Witt vector sheaf is taken sectionwise.
Existence, uniqueness and regularity of t are proved locally by Theorem 6.5(i) on affinoid perfectoid U (see the next node); before that the definition of B_dR is only provisional.
proofSteps: Sheaves are defined by the displayed formulas; B_inf = A_inf[1/p], the ideal sheaves (ker θ)^n and the inverse limit defining B_dR^+ are formed in sheaves on X_proet.
acceptance: On an affinoid perfectoid U with Û = Spa(R, R^+) these sheaves have sections A_inf(R, R^+), B_inf(R, R^+), B_dR^+(R, R^+), B_dR(R, R^+) (Theorem 6.5).
gr^i B_dR ≅ Ô_X(i) globally on X_proet (Proposition 6.7).

nodes.title: Values and acyclicity of the period sheaves on affinoid perfectoids; profinite covers; gr^i B_dR = Ô_X(i)
nodes.statement: (Theorem 6.5 and Corollary 6.6) Let X be locally noetherian over Spa(K, K^+), K perfectoid of characteristic 0 with open bounded valuation subring K^+, and U ∈ X_proet affinoid perfectoid with Û = Spa(R, R^+). (i) A_inf(U) = A_inf(R, R^+), and likewise for B_inf, B_dR^+, B_dR; in particular ξ generates Fil^1 B_dR^+(U), is unique up to a unit and is not a zero-divisor. (ii) H^i(U, F) is almost zero for i > 0 for each of these sheaves (almost setting relative to A_inf(K, K^+) and the ideal generated by all [π^{1/p^N}]). (iii) [π] is invertible in B_dR^+(U) and B_dR(U), so their higher cohomology vanishes outright. (Corollary 6.6) For a profinite set S and V = U × S, F(V) = Hom_cont(S, F(U)) for F among Ô_X^+, Ô_X, Ô^+_{X♭}, Ô_{X♭}, A_inf, B_inf, B_dR^+, B_dR, gr^i B_dR, with the natural inverse/direct limit and quotient topologies. (Proposition 6.7, for X locally noetherian over Spa(Q_p, Z_p)) gr^i B_dR ≅ Ô_X(i) on X_proet, where (i) is the Tate twist by Ẑ_p(1) = lim μ_{p^n}.

Then X_i ↦ u_i defines an isomorphism B_dR^+|_X̃[[X_1, ..., X_n]] → OB_dR^+|_X̃ of sheaves on X_proet/X̃. Strengthened form (erratum): for U ∈ X_proet/X̃_K affinoid perfectoid with (R, R^+) as above and i sufficiently large, the ker θ-adic completion S_i of (R_i^+ ⊗̂_{W(κ)} A_inf(R, R^+))[1/p] is isomorphic to B_dR^+(R, R^+)[[X_1, ..., X_n]] via the constructed map, independently of i, so OB_dR^+(U) = B_dR^+(R, R^+)[[X_1, ..., X_n]].

Lemma 6.11: for a perfectoid affinoid (K, O_K)-algebra (R, R^+) and a finitely generated O_k-algebra S, any f: S → B_dR^+(R, R^+)[[X]] with θ(f(S)) ⊂ R^+ extends to the p-adic completion of S. Hensel's lemma for the ker θ-adically complete ring B_dR^+(U)[[X]] with residue ring Ô_X(U).

For affinoid perfectoid U = lim U_i over X̃_K, apply Lemma 6.12 to U_i → T^n, lift the etale algebras R_{i0} uniquely by Hensel's lemma to B_dR^+(U)[[X]], extend to the p-adic completions R_i^+ by Lemma 6.11, and take direct limits: this gives an O_X|_X̃_K-algebra structure on B_dR^+|_X̃_K[[X]] compatible with the reduction B_dR^+[[X]]/(ker θ) = Ô_X and sending T_i to [T_i♭] + X_i.

nodes.title: The relative Poincare lemma, Griffiths transversality, strict exactness, Faltings's extension and gr^• OB_dR
nodes.statement: For X smooth of dimension n over Spa(k, O_k), the sequence 0 → B_dR^+ → OB_dR^+ → OB_dR^+ ⊗_{O_X} Ω^1_X → ... → OB_dR^+ ⊗_{O_X} Ω^n_X → 0 of sheaves on X_proet is exact; ∇ satisfies Griffiths transversality ∇(Fil^i) ⊂ Fil^{i-1} ⊗ Ω^1, and with Ω^i_X in degree i the sequence is strict exact for the filtrations. Consequently (Faltings's extension) 0 → Ô_X(1) → gr^1 OB_dR^+ → Ô_X ⊗_{O_X} Ω^1_X → 0 is exact, and over X_proet/X̃_K, gr^i OB_dR ≅ ξ^i Ô_X[X_1/ξ, ..., X_n/ξ], so gr^• OB_dR ≅ Ô_X[ξ^{±1}, X_1, ..., X_n] with ξ and X_i in degree 1.

nodes.title: Cohomology of gr^i OB_dR on affinoids with a toric etale chart; ν_* OB_dR = O_{X_et} and R^1 ν_* Ô_X(1) = Ω^1
nodes.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R^+) be affinoid of finite type over Spa(k, O_k) with an etale map X → T^n which is a composite of rational embeddings and finite etale maps. (i) If K contains all p-power roots of unity, H^q(X_K, gr^0 OB_dR) = 0 for q > 0 and equals R ⊗̂_k K for q = 0. (ii) H^q(X, gr^i OB_dR) = 0 unless i = 0 and q ∈ {0, 1}; (gr^0 OB_dR)(X) = R and H^1(X, gr^0 OB_dR) = R · log χ, χ the cyclotomic character. Consequently, for X smooth over Spa(k, O_k): ν_* OB_dR = O_{X_et}, ν_* Ô_X = O_{X_et}, ν_* Ô_X(n) = 0 for n ≥ 1, R^1 ν_* Ô_X(1) ≅ Ω^1_{X_et} via the connecting map of Faltings's extension, R^1 ν_* Ô_X(n) = 0 for n ≥ 2; more generally (Remark 6.20, stated without proof) R^i ν_* Ô_X(j) = Ω^j_{X_et} for i = j, Ω^j_{X_et} log χ for i = j + 1, and 0 otherwise. The source prints "Ω^i_{X_et} log χ if i = j + 1", which is a misprint: Proposition 6.16(ii) and the graded Poincaré sequences give Rν_* Ô_X(j) ≅ Ω^j[−j] ⊕ Ω^j log χ[−j−1], and for j = 0 the printed formula would give R^1ν_* Ô_X = Ω^1 log χ instead of O_{X_et} log χ.
hypotheses: X affinoid of finite type over Spa(k, O_k) with the stated toric etale chart; K = completion of k(μ_{p^∞}) in (ii), Γ_k = Gal(k(μ_{p^∞})/k).

Inputs: Cartan-Leray for the Z_p^n-cover X̃_K → X_K whose fibre products are affinoid perfectoid (so the higher cohomology of the sheaves vanishes there); Corollary 6.6 for gr^0 OB_dR; Lemma 6.17 (γ_i(V_j) = V_j + δ_{ij} for V_i = t^{-1} log([T_i♭]/T_i)); Lemma 6.18 (R^+ ⊗̂_{O_k⟨T^{±1}⟩} O_K⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ → R̃^+ injective with p-power-torsion cokernel, from Lemma 4.5(ii)); Lemma 5.5 (continuous Z_p^n-cohomology of the perfectoid torus via the Koszul complex, with the cokernel of ∧^q R_0^n → H^q_cont(Z_p^n, R) killed by ζ_p − 1 and compatibility with base change); Brinon [5] Proposition 4.1.2 (unread); Tate's computation of H^q_cont(Γ_k, Q_p(i)) ([19], unread). Further asserted steps: that R(i) → R ⊗̂_k K(i) induces an isomorphism on continuous Γ_k-cohomology ("similarly to Lemma 5.5"; a Tate-type descent for K = completion of k(μ_{p^∞}), not a consequence of Lemma 5.5); that "the version of Corollary 6.6 for gr^0 OB_dR stays true"; the formula H^q(X_K^{m/X}, gr^i OB_dR) = Hom_cont(Γ_k^{m−1}, H^q(X_K, gr^i OB_dR)) ("inspection of the proof"); and, in Corollary 6.19, local existence on smooth X of etale maps to T^n factoring as composites of rational embeddings and finite etale maps, as Proposition 6.16 requires.
proofSteps: (i) H^q(X_K, gr^0 OB_dR) = H^q_cont(Z_p^n, gr^0 OB_dR(X̃_K)) with gr^0 OB_dR(X̃_K) = R̃[V_1, ..., V_n]; the inclusion (R ⊗̂_k K)[V] ⊂ R̃[V] induces an isomorphism on continuous cohomology (check on the associated graded for the polynomial degree, where Z_p^n acts trivially on the V_i, and use Lemma 6.18 with Lemma 5.5 for R ⊗̂ K ⊂ R̃).
Compute H^q_cont(Z_p^n, (R ⊗̂ K)[V]) inductively: γ_i − 1 acts on S[V_i] by P ↦ P(V_i + 1) − P(V_i), with kernel the constants and trivial cokernel.

(ii) All gr^i OB_dR are isomorphic to gr^0 on X_proet/X_K; for the cover X_K → X with Γ_k-fibre products, H^q(X_K^{m/X}, gr^i OB_dR) = Hom_cont(Γ_k^{m-1}, H^q(X_K, gr^i OB_dR)), giving H^q(X, gr^i OB_dR) = H^q_cont(Γ_k, R ⊗̂_k K(i)) = R ⊗_{Q_p} H^q_cont(Γ_k, Q_p(i)) (the map R(i) → R ⊗̂ K(i) is asserted to be a Γ_k-cohomology isomorphism "similarly to Lemma 5.5"; see hypotheses), and Tate's computation of the latter.

Corollary 6.19: after inverting t the Poincare lemma gives 0 → B_dR → OB_dR → ..., whose 0-th graded piece injects ν_* Ô_X into ν_* gr^0 OB_dR = O_{X_et}; the graded pieces 0 → Ô_X(n) → gr^n OB_dR → gr^{n-1} OB_dR ⊗ Ω^1 → ... give the vanishing and the identification of R^1 ν_* Ô_X(1). "The first part is clear" (ν_* OB_dR = O_{X_et}) and the identification with the boundary map of Faltings's extension ("one directly checks") are not argued.
acceptance: For X = T^n over k, H^1(X, gr^0 OB_dR) = k⟨T^{±1}⟩ log χ and R^1 ν_* Ô_X(1) = Ω^1 with basis dT_i/T_i.
